newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower on spillover.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower on spillover.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended lower on spillover from CBOT corn and soybeans and on feelings the market rose too far too fast in Wednesday's closing rally, traders said.
Spring wheat aped CBOT grains and oilseeds when it dropped late in response to crop production estimates included in President Clinton's proposed budget for 1998.

Earlier, March had drawn support from USDA's weekly export sales report, which said net wheat export sales totaled 408,800 tonnes during the week ended January 30. That was above expectations of 150,000 to 250,000 tonnes.
Traders said March wheat had also been buoyed by strong cash basis levels in the Pacific Northwest, and by the limited amount of farmer sales of spring wheat.
The MGE March/May spread continued to widen despite the late break in values. The spread traded out to 20 cents Thursday compared to 19 cents late Wednesday.
MGE spring wheat settled two to 4-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with March down 2-1/2 cents at $3.85-1/2. March had risen as high as $3.89-3/4 during the session.
Traders said Atwood-Peavey was a featured player, selling 2.5 million May bushels on the spread with KCBT May wheat.
MGE barley did not trade and closed unchanged.
